analysis.title: Nordic Alert: Stocks fell on AI concerns, ECB and BoJ on hold
key_insights: US stocks fell on 10/29 (S&P 500 -0.3%, Nasdaq -1.4%) after lower-than-expected results from Alphabet and others, adding to concerns about AI sector valuations.
The risk-off move sent investors into Treasuries, the Swiss franc and the Japanese yen.
Crude oil rose after media reports suggested the US may resume military strikes against Iran. The WSJ reported the president was notified of possible future military options.
Gold fell below $4,000 per ounce and was on track for its lowest close since mid-July. The euro strengthened against the dollar.
The ECB held rates unchanged with no forward commitments. SEB says nothing in the decision or press release rules out another rate hike in December.
Christine Lagarde announced she will resign in February 2027.
The BoJ left rates unchanged, as widely expected, but its forecasts were relatively hawkish and kept inflation risks tilted to the upside after the September hike.
The BoJ assessed underlying inflation as 'broadly consistent' with the 2% target for the first time since the target was introduced in 2013.
Japan's October core inflation printed at 2.6%, slightly below expectations.

Israel's election produced no majority for Netanyahu's coalition or the main opposition alliance. Several weeks of political uncertainty are likely, with Netanyahu staying on as acting prime minister.

SEB's investor survey shows most respondents expect a Riksbank hike next week, almost all expect the rate at or above 2% in December, and 95% expect at least 50 basis points of hikes by March compared with today.
Euro area flash October inflation and Q3 GDP are due on 10/30, along with the ECB Survey of Professional Forecasters.
